scope: Sparse rounded granite uplands with optional steep joint faces, generated as part of existing terrain.
status: Core scalar and actual-world checks passed; native rendering and performance pending.

sources.use: Granitic joint patterns and exfoliation produce rounded summits and steep fractured faces.
Granitic uplands can retain forest around exposed rock masses; do not restrict all prominent bedrock to deserts.

placement: Granitic bedrock predominance, substantial relief, low sediment cover, nonmarsh and nonsaline ground.
Exclude current icefields, ocean and immediately coastal source cells.
Sparse physical-area sampling inside coherent geological provinces; not one monument per biome or noise crest.
rendering: Existing terrain mesh, lithology layers and indexed finite footprints.
No new scenery objects, materials, alpha foliage, texture samples, draw calls or frame tick.
Rock exposure suppresses mature rooted vegetation, with a smooth finite foot and no bare disk behind a cut face.
limits: Heightfield approximation cannot represent an overhang, detached slab or cave.
Static landform, not a tectonic uplift, erosion or historical glacier simulation.
Existing rock textures are reused; native visual acceptance is still required.
